Lipid accumulation, glucose metabolism, glycogen storage, transcriptomic changes, and adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT) signaling were assessed using biochemical assays, staining, reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), western blotting, RNA sequencing, and detection of inflammatory activity. In PA-treated HepG2 cells, NaB reduced lipid accumulation, improved glucose uptake and glycogen storage, and reduced the secretion of the pro-inflammatory mediators tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) in a dose-dependent manner. These effects were accompanied by the restoration of G protein-coupled receptor 43 (GPR43)/calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase 2 (CaMKK2)/AMPKα/sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) signaling and the activation of PI3K/AKT signaling, with decreased lipogenesis, enhanced fatty acid oxidation, reduced gluconeogenic gene expression, and alleviation of the cellular inflammatory response. In HFD-fed mice, NaB reduced body weight gain, improved serum and hepatic lipid profiles, attenuated hepatic steatosis, improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity, and increased hepatic glycogen storage, while markedly lowering circulating and intrahepatic pro-inflammatory cytokine levels and downregulating hepatic expression of the macrophage marker F4/80 to mitigate inflammatory infiltration of the liver. These results demonstrate that NaB administration alleviated hepatic steatosis and IR in MASLD models, with these effects coinciding with the coordinated regulation of AMPK and PI3K/AKT signaling. While NaB may serve as a metabolic modulator, further mechanistic validation of dual-pathway crosstalk, characterization of inflammatory responses, and translational research are still needed.

title: Five Trials, Five Different Questions: Design Heterogeneity Among Lipoprotein(a)-Lowering Cardiovascular Outcomes Trials After Lp(a)HORIZON.
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), widely regarded as causal on the basis of genetic and epidemiological evidence, for which no approved Lp(a)-lowering therapy exists. In September 2026, Novartis announced that Lp(a)HORIZON, evaluating the antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) pelacarsen and the most clinically advanced of five phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trials (CVOTs) targeting Lp(a), had not met its primary composite endpoint. Key details, including the magnitude of Lp(a) lowering achieved, the result in the pre-specified higher-Lp(a) subpopulation, the effect estimate, and the safety profile, remain unpublished pending congress presentation. This review compares the design of all five phase 3 Lp(a)-lowering CVOTs, identified through a curated bibliography, a PubMed search for design and rationale publications, and searches of the ClinicalTrials.gov registry, and situates them within the wider landscape of Lp(a)-directed therapy. The four trials still running are not replications of the first. They differ from Lp(a)HORIZON and from one another in mechanism (ASO, small interfering RNA (siRNA), or oral small molecule), dosing interval, Lp(a) eligibility threshold, sample size, stage of disease at which they intervene, and, critically, in the composition of the primary endpoint: the two olpasiran trials use a coronary-only composite that excludes stroke, whereas Lp(a)HORIZON and, by its own nomenclature, MOVE-Lp(a) include it. A coronary-only composite and a stroke-inclusive composite do not estimate the same quantity, so effect estimates from these trials cannot be directly compared without accounting for endpoint composition, population, and follow-up. Five non-exclusive explanations for the neutral result are set out, together with the evidence bearing on each and what would distinguish them. A single neutral trial does not resolve the Lp(a) question, and the readouts expected between 2027 and 2031 will not resolve it jointly unless these design differences are held in view when the results are compared.

title: Quercetin modulates key biomarkers and inhibits cell proliferation in endometriosis.
abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic disorder and the present study investigated the therapeutic potential of quercetin, derived from Paeoniae Radix Alba and Hedysarum multijugum Maxim (BSHQ), by identifying bioactive ingredients and key biomarkers with a focus on their molecular interactions in the context of endometriosis. The present study identified 32 bioactive ingredients from BSHQ, linked to 231 target genes. Gene Expression Omnibus datasets and Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis were used to analyze differentially expressed genes and key co-expression modules. In vitro assays, including half-maximal inhibitory concentration, Cell Counting Kit-8 and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine assays, assessed the impact of quercetin on cell proliferation in endometriosis cell lines. Molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analyzed the interaction of quercetin with biomarkers. The present study identified 16 BSHQ-related genes. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis showed distinct expression patterns of these genes in various cell types. Molecular docking confirmed strong binding between quercetin and these biomarkers. In vitro assays revealed quercetin markedly inhibited the proliferation of endometriosis cell lines, reducing cell proliferation and serpin family E member 1 (SERPINE1) expression. CETSA showed that quercetin can directly bind to SERPINE1 protein and enhance its thermal stability against temperature-induced degradation, a post-translational effect independent of expression regulation, and SPR analysis further supported the direct interaction between quercetin and SERPINE1. Furthermore, SERPINE1 overexpression rescued the inhibitory effects of quercetin on proliferation, highlighting its critical role in mediating the effects of quercetin in endometriosis. The present study underscored SERPINE1 as a pivotal biomarker in endometriosis and revealed that quercetin effectively modulated key disease mechanisms, offering promising therapeutic potential. These findings provide a solid basis for future research aimed at exploring the role of quercetin in the treatment of endometriosis.

title: DJ-1 regulates glioblastoma proliferation and apoptosis by modulating UBA52 mediated NF-κB signaling pathway.
abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most lethal and treatment-resistant malignant solid tumor​ worldwide. Conventional therapy consisting of surgical resection with chemoradiotherapy yields unsatisfactory outcomes, highlighting an urgent demand for novel therapeutic targets. DJ-1 is a multifunctional protein involved in tumor progression, yet its biological function and molecular mechanism in GBM remain poorly defined. DJ-1 expression was initially evaluated utilizing data from TCGA and GTEx databases, IHC and western blot in GBM tissues and cell lines. A short hairpin RNA targeting DJ-1 (shDJ-1) was constructed and transfected into GBM cell lines. Functional assays were performed to assess the effects of DJ‑1 on GBM cell proliferation and apoptosis. Proteomic sequencing was applied to screen potential downstream effectors of DJ-1. Immunofluorescence co-localization was performed to confirm the subcellular localization of DJ-1 and UBA52. The expression of UBA52 and NF-κB pathway-related proteins were detected by Western blot. Rescue experiments were conducted by overexpressing UBA52 in DJ‑1 knockdown GBM cells. A subcutaneous xenograft model in immunodeficient nude mice was established to evaluate the in vivo effect of DJ-1 silencing on tumor growth. DJ-1 was significantly elevated in GBM tissues and cell lines, with higher levels correlating with unfavorable prognosis in patients. Functionally, DJ-1 knockdown substantially suppressed cell proliferation and promoted apoptosis in GBM cells. Mechanistically, UBA52 was identified as a critical downstream target of DJ-1, with UBA52 overexpression mitigating the tumor suppressive effects caused by DJ-1 depletion in GBM progression. Moreover, DJ-1 knockdown inactivated the NF-κB signaling pathway by downregulating UBA52. In vivo experiments further confirmed that DJ-1 silencing significantly impeded tumor growth in nude mice. The present study elucidates that DJ-1 facilitates GBM progression by modulating the UBA52/NF-κB signaling axis. These findings suggest that targeting DJ-1 may represent a novel promising therapeutic strategy for GBM.

title: Epigenetic dysregulation in Clear cell renal cell carcinoma: from mechanisms to precision medicine.
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is a paradigm of epigenetic dysregulation. The characteristic loss of chromosome 3p leads to the inactivation of a constellation of pivotal epigenetic regulators, including PBRM1, SETD2, and BAP1, reshaping the epigenome across multiple layers. This review synthesizes the major epigenetic alterations in ccRCC, encompassing aberrations in chromatin structure, dysregulation of DNA and RNA methylation, deregulated noncoding RNAs, and the accumulation of oncometabolites. Collectively, these changes drive oncogene activation, tumor suppressor silencing, genomic instability, and metabolic reprogramming. We also evaluate the clinical potential of these epigenetic alterations. First, they can serve as noninvasive diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, particularly through the analysis of DNA methylomes and exosomes in liquid biopsies. Second, these alterations enable a therapeutic strategy-epigenetic synthetic lethality-which exploits vulnerabilities induced by the loss of VHL, BAP1, SETD2, and PBRM1. Such vulnerabilities are selectively targetable by PARP, ATR, or EZH2 inhibitors, thereby offering a novel framework for precision medicine in ccRCC. Finally, we outline future research directions, including dissecting intra-tumoral epigenetic heterogeneity, defining functional epigenetic biomarkers, expanding next-generation epigenetic therapeutics, targeting the metabo-epigenetic circuitry, and rationally integrating epigenetic modulators with immunotherapies and HIF-2α inhibitors, aiming to translate epigenetic knowledge into improved clinical outcomes.

title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface. Shared disease-associated genes were identified using integrated bioinformatics and protein-protein interaction network analysis, followed by analyses of TCGA and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Deep learning-based (DeepPurpose) and structure-based (AutoDock Vina) virtual screening were used to prioritize multi-target ligands. Binding was assessed by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and molecular dynamics simulations. Cellular effects were evaluated in a diabetic-mimetic model using high glucose, insulin, and palmitic acid (three factors; TF), with HCT116 cells and THP-1-derived macrophages. The IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis was prioritized as a candidate inflammatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface. TCGA and single-cell RNA-seq analyses associated axis-related expression with immune infiltration and macrophage polarization-related transcriptional signatures; higher axis expression was also associated with longer overall survival. Hupehenine (HU), a steroidal alkaloid, was identified as a multi-target ligand engaging IL1β, CXCL8, and CXCR2. SPR showed concentration-dependent binding (KD: CXCR2, 505 nM; CXCL8, 2.2 μM; IL1β, 12.7 μM) and interference with CXCL8-CXCR2 binding. In a diabetic-mimetic model, HU reduced HCT116 cell viability, migration, and invasion. TF-conditioned cells were more sensitive to HU than non-TF cells, whereas a corresponding increase in sensitivity was not observed for 5-fluorouracil or oxaliplatin. HU also decreased M2-associated and increased M1-associated macrophage markers. These findings support the IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis as a candidate immunomodulatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface and identify HU as an in vitro multi-target ligand. The observed changes in macrophage markers and differential sensitivity under diabetic-mimetic conditions warrant further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation, including direct assessment of macrophage function.

title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root.
abstract: Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

title: Promotion of the Proliferation and Migration of Breast Cancer Cells by the Micro Ribonucleic Acid miR-425-5p via Dihydropyrimidinase-Like 2.
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most common malignant tumor in women. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a class of noncoding single-stranded RNA molecules that are closely related to the development, progression, and metastasis of BC. The miRNA miR-425-5p is upregulated in a variety of cancers and can promote cancer progression. This study aimed to investigate the role of miR-425-5p in BC and its molecular mechanism. The expression of miR-425-5p in BC was analyzed using the Cancer Genome Atlas database and two Gene Expression Omnibus validation cohorts. Expression of miR-425-5p in paired BC and adjacent nontumor tissues from four patients with invasive ductal carcinoma and in normal breast epithelial and BC cell lines. Expression of miR-425-5p in BC tissues and cell lines was detected via quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Protein expression was detected using a Western blot. Cell growth and proliferation were assessed via a 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay. A transwell assay was used to detect the migration ability of BC cells. The effects of miR-425-5p and DPYSL2 were verified using patient-derived BC organoids established from the four tumor samples, as well as xenograft experiments in female nude mice randomly divided into three groups (five or eight mice per group). The experimental results showed that miR-425-5p expression levels were higher in tumor tissue than in normal tissue. The RT-qPCR results showed high expression of miR-425-5p in clinical samples and BC cell lines; miR-425-5p promoted the growth and migration of BC cells and targeted and degraded the DPYSL2 messenger RNA. The DPYSL2 protein content decreased upon miR-425-5p overexpression. The MTT and Transwell assay results indicated that miR-425-5p regulated BC progression via DPYSL2. Inhibition of miR-425-5p or overexpression of DPYSL2 inhibited BC growth in organoid and nude mouse xenograft experiments. In summary, miR-425-5p promoted BC development by targeting DPYSL2.

title: LINC00520 Regulates VDAC1 Oligomerization to Promote Cisplatin Resistance in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy remains the primary treatment for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), although its efficacy is frequently limited by acquired cisplatin resistance. The involvement of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in this resistance is not well understood. Differentially expressed lncRNAs were identified through bioinformatics analysis. LINC00520 expression was further validated in LUAD clinical specimens and cisplatin (CDDP)-resistant A549 cells. MS2-tagged RNA affinity purification (MS2-TRAP) coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) was used to screen for LINC00520-interacting proteins, which were subsequently validated by RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP). Functional assays, including Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), colony formation, and apoptosis analysis, were conducted. Voltage-dependent anion-selective channel protein 1 (VDAC1) oligomerization and mitochondrial apoptosis were assessed by western blotting and 5,5',6,6'-tetrachloro-1,1',3,3'-tetraethylbenzimidazolylcarbocyanine iodide (JC-1) staining. In vivo xenograft models were used to corroborate key findings. LINC00520 was markedly upregulated in LUAD tissues and A549/CDDP-resistant cells, and elevated expression correlated with poor prognosis. Functionally, LINC00520 promoted proliferation, suppressed apoptosis, and enhanced cisplatin resistance, whereas its knockdown restored chemosensitivity. Mechanistically, LINC00520 directly bound VDAC1 and inhibited its oligomerization, thereby suppressing mitochondrial apoptosis. In vivo, LINC00520 silencing suppressed tumor growth and partially restored cisplatin sensitivity. LINC00520 drives cisplatin resistance in LUAD by modulating VDAC1-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis, suggesting that LINC00520 may represent a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for reversing cisplatin resistance in LUAD.

title: Irisin Protects Against Seawater Aspiration-Induced Acute Lung Injury via Inhibiting JAK2/STAT1 Signal Pathway.
abstract: Seawater aspiration-induced acute lung injury (SW-ALI) is a life-threatening inflammatory disorder with no specific pharmacological treatment. Irisin, an exercise-induced peptide, modulates inflammation, but its role in SW-ALI remains undefined. This study aims to investigate the protective effects and mechanisms of irisin against SW-ALI. A murine model of SW-ALI was established in C57BL/6 mice via intratracheal seawater, followed by intraperitoneal administration of irisin. Pulmonary function was assessed using whole-body plethysmography (WBP). Lung injury severity was evaluated by histology, lung index and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) protein concentration and cell counts. Immune infiltration and p-STAT1 nuclear translocation were detected by immunofluorescence. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) identified transcriptomic alterations and signaling pathways in lung tissues, validated by RT-qPCR and ELISA. In vitro, seawater-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were used to evaluate inflammatory responses and JAK2/STAT1 signaling. A JAK2 activator coumermycin A1(CA) was employed to verify the necessity of the pathway. Irisin improved respiratory function, reduced lung index, BALF protein levels and cell counts, and alleviated lung pathology in SW-ALI mice. RNA-seq revealed that irisin reprogrammed pulmonary gene expression, suppressing inflammatory and immune pathways, specifically downregulating the expression and secretion of inflammation-related molecules, including chemokines (CXCL9, CXCL10), interferons (IFN-β), and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) both in vivo and in vitro. Concurrently, irisin attenuated seawater-induced infiltration of neutrophils and M1-like macrophages in lung tissues, and suppressed M1-like polarization of seawater-stimulated RAW264.7 cells. Mechanistically, irisin inhibited JAK2/STAT1 phosphorylation and p-STAT1 nuclear translocation. Furthermore, CA-mediated JAK2 activation partially abrogated irisin's suppression of M1-like polarization, inflammation-related molecules release, and p-STAT1 nuclear translocation. Irisin alleviates SW-ALI, involving the inhibition of the JAK2/STAT1 pathway, which suppresses M1-like macrophage polarization and the subsequent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and type I interferons, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for SW-ALI.

title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Analysis Identifies Ion Channel-Related Biomarkers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
abstract: Human ion channel genes (HICGs), as core effectors of transmembrane signal transduction, play a critical role in the initiation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of ion channel genes in COPD. Differential expression analysis was performed to screen HICGs in COPD datasets. A total of 107 machine learning models were employed to identify hub HICGs and evaluate their diagnostic performance, and SHAP analysis was used to assess feature contributions. GSEA, immune cell infiltration, and inflammatory cytokine correlation analyses were conducted on the hub HICGs. Consensus clustering and WGCNA were used to define two disease subtypes and key modules. Single-cell RNA-seq data were used to examine the expression patterns of the hub HICGs. Subsequently, virtual knockout, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were performed. The nine hub HICGs showed high diagnostic performance in cross-dataset validation, with LRRC8D ranking first in the SHAP analysis. These HICGs were significantly correlated with immune cells and inflammatory cytokines. Consensus clustering revealed significant gender differences between the two subtypes (BH-adjusted P = 0.01), and the two subtypes were enriched in phagocytosis and MAPK signaling pathways, respectively. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis using the Ro/e index suggested enrichment of macrophages and a reduction in smooth muscle cells in the disease group. Virtual knockout of LRRC8D was predicted to preferentially affect CD68 and the affected genes were enriched in human cytomegalovirus infection. Virtual screening prioritized Tezacaftor as a potential therapeutic agent, and molecular docking predicted that Tezacaftor may exhibit high binding affinity for the hub HICGs. We identified potential HICGs in COPD and suggested a potential role for LRRC8D, as well as the potential utility of hub HICGs in disease subtyping, particularly with respect to gender, and Tezacaftor may serve as a candidate therapeutic agent.
extra: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis

title: TWEAK signaling drives the transition from psoriasis to atopic dermatitis-like inflammation in paradoxical eczema.
abstract: Targeted biologics have transformed the treatment of inflammatory skin diseases such as plaque psoriasis. However, some patients with psoriasis paradoxically develop eczematous skin reactions after therapy targeting tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin-17 (IL-17), or IL-23. Although paradoxical eczema (PE) resembles atopic dermatitis (AD) clinically and histologically, the molecular mechanisms that drive its development remain poorly understood. Here, we generated high-resolution cellular and spatial maps of human skin using single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, and in vitro assays, profiling lesional biopsies from patients with PE (n = 8 donors), alongside healthy control, psoriasis, and AD skin (n = 4 donors per group). In PE, we identified distinct transcriptional changes characterized by myeloid and T cell expansion and an altered keratinocyte phenotype shaped by TNF-like weak inducer of apoptosis (TWEAK; encoded by TNFSF12) signaling through its receptor TNFRSF12A, confirmed at the protein level by immunohistochemistry. To define the underlying mechanism, we stimulated immortalized (N-TERT) and primary human keratinocytes and found that TWEAK acted together with IL-13 to drive a T helper 2- and type I interferon-polarized epithelial program that partially recapitulated the keratinocyte signature of PE lesions. We validated key target genes by quantitative polymerase chain reaction in primary keratinocytes. In THP-1 cells and primary human CD14+ monocytes, anti-TNF treatment induced TWEAK expression, suggesting a compensatory inflammatory circuit. Together, these findings identify the TWEAK-IL-13 axis as a key driver of PE and suggest how cytokine blockade may reshape cutaneous immune responses.

title: Development of a novel RNA modification-based risk model to predict prognosis and immunotherapy response in melanoma using machine learning.
abstract: Melanoma is a highly malignant cancer that poses a significant global health burden, yet there is limited ability to predict prognosis or immunotherapy efficacy for melanomas. Emerging evidence highlights the role of RNA modification regulators (m6A, m1A, m5C, and m7G) in modulating oncogenesis and immune responses. We comprehensively profiled 84 regulators of RNA modification (m6A/m1A/m5C/m7G) across multiple melanoma cohorts. Unsupervised clustering was performed to identify RNA modification-based subtypes, followed by WGCNA to reveal key modules. We developed the RMODscore prognostic model using LASSO and multivariate Cox regression and validated the model in several independent melanoma immunotherapy cohorts. Finally, we explored the association of RMODscore with immune signatures and drug sensitivity. We found significant differences in survival among three different RNA modification subtypes and identified the ME13 module as significantly associated with these subtypes using the WGCNA method. Our newly constructed 10-gene RMODscore model showed strong predictive performance in the TCGA cohort and four independent immunotherapy datasets. A high RMODscore was associated with poor survival, immune-cold phenotypes, and resistance to checkpoint blockade. Functional analysis revealed that tumors with high RMODscore values exhibited upregulation of proliferation-related pathways, whereas tumors with low RMODscore values exhibited greater immune activation. In addition, the RMODscore predicted sensitivity to ERK and JNK inhibitors, suggesting potential drug repurposing strategies. This study presents a novel RNA modification-based prognostic risk score as a robust prognostic tool for melanoma which may provide potential prognostic stratification value. These findings highlight the potential of RNA modification signatures for prognostic stratification and may provide preliminary insights for future therapeutic strategy exploration in patients with melanoma.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis and Experimental Validation Identify ATF3 as a Mesangial Cell-Associated Candidate Regulator in IgA Nephropathy.
abstract: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is an immune-mediated glomerular disease marked by mesangial proliferation, inflammation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and progressive renal injury. This study aimed to identify IgAN-associated genes and evaluate the relevance of activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) to mesangial cell activation. Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression, co-expression network, machine learning, and immune infiltration analyses. Single-cell RNA sequencing, mesangial cell-specific high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and single-cell regulatory network inference were used to assess cell type-specific expression and regulatory activity. The findings were further evaluated using Nephroseq and an aggregated IgA1-stimulated human mesangial cell model with ATF3 knockdown. Integrated analysis identified 47 shared differentially expressed genes and a 12-gene candidate set with reduced expression in IgAN. ATF3 was prioritized as a mesangial cell-associated candidate and showed reduced expression and regulon activity in the analyzed single-cell dataset. Nephroseq analysis showed lower glomerular ATF3 expression in IgAN-related kidney disease samples; ATF3 expression was positively associated with estimated glomerular filtration rate and negatively associated with serum creatinine and proteinuria. Aggregated IgA1 reduced ATF3 expression in human mesangial cells, whereas ATF3 knockdown further increased inflammatory cytokine expression and proliferative activity. Reduced ATF3 expression is associated with IgAN-related mesangial cell activation. ATF3 may represent a mesangial cell-associated candidate regulator that warrants further mechanistic and clinical validation.

title: Lack of differential sperm acrosome-associated 1 gene expression between X- and Y-bearing spermatozoa in Bali bulls (Bos javanicus domesticus).
abstract: This study aimed to determine whether the sperm acrosome-associated 1 (SPACA1) gene exhibits differential expression between X- and Y-bearing spermatozoa of Bali bulls and assess its potential as an RNA biomarker for sperm sexing. Sexed frozen semen (X or Y fractions) from Bali bulls was obtained from the Singosari National Artificial Insemination Center, Malang, Indonesia. Post-thaw semen quality was evaluated for motility, viability, abnormality, concentration, and plasma membrane integrity. Total RNA was extracted separately from X and Y fractions using easy-BLUE reagent, and SPACA1 expression was quantified by RT-qPCR using GAPDH as an internal control. Relative expression was calculated by the 2-ΔΔCt method, and group differences were analyzed with the Mann-Whitney U test. The SPACA1 expression was numerically higher in X-bearing than Y-bearing spermatozoa (1.00 versus 0.51), but the difference was not significant. Thus, SPACA1 transcripts do not provide a reliable molecular marker for sperm sex differentiation. Future work should focus on protein-level characterization of SPACA1 and exploration of sex-biased surface proteins for immunological sexing. This research supports Sustainable Development Goal 2: Zero Hunger, by contributing to reproductive efficiency in livestock, and Sustainable Development Goal 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, through development of cost-effective, sustainable sperm sexing technologies.
authors: Intan Firdha Olien Noor Al Ichsan

title: Smad4 Regulates the Developmental Coordination of Cortical Neurons via the CXCL12-CXCR4 Axis.
abstract: The functional assembly of neural circuits during cortical development relies on the precise spatiotemporal coordination of excitatory projection neurons and inhibitory interneurons. Here, we show that SMAD family member 4 (SMAD4) is required for this developmental coordination. We performed conditional deletion of Smad4 in pallial progenitors and evaluated the spatial distribution and number of Glutamic acid decarboxylase 67-green fluorescent protein positive (Gad67-GFP+) interneurons in the embryonic and adult cortex. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was utilized to assess transcriptomic changes in the Smad4-deficient cortex. Further in vivo expression validation and functional assessments were conducted using a C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12 (Cxcl12)-Discosoma red fluorescent protein (DsRed) reporter line and Cxcl12 loss-of-function mutants, respectively. Conditional deletion of Smad4 in pallial progenitors disrupts the spatial distribution and overall number of Gad67-GFP+ interneurons in both the embryonic and adult cortex. scRNA-seq revealed a marked reduction in Cxcl12 expression within the mutant cortex, while its receptor, C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4 (Cxcr4), remained normally expressed in interneurons. We confirmed this downregulation in vivo using the Cxcl12-DsRed reporter line. Functionally, Cxcl12 loss-of-function mutants phenocopy the interneuron migration deficits seen in Smad4 mutants. Our results uncover a projection neuron-derived SMAD4-CXCL12 signaling cascade that regulates CXCR4-dependent interneuron migration, providing a molecular basis for the cross-talk between these two distinct neuronal lineages.

title: Prognostic Value of the Blood Urea Nitrogen-to-Fibrinogen Ratio for 30-Day Mortality in Patients with Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease associated with substantial mortality. Renal dysfunction and coagulation abnormalities are closely related to disease severity. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of the blood urea nitrogen-to-fibrinogen ratio (BUN/FIB) in patients with SFTS. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients with laboratory-confirmed SFTS admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of the University of Science and Technology of China between June 2020 and June 2025. Admission BUN/FIB was calculated using BUN and fibrinogen values. Logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, survival analysis, and paired-sample analysis were performed to evaluate the association between BUN/FIB and 30-day all-cause mortality. Of the 475 patients, 378 (79.6%) survived and 97 (20.4%) died. Admission BUN/FIB levels were significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors. Multivariable logistic regression identified older age, neurological signs, higher C-reactive protein, higher Ct-derived SFTSV RNA burden, and higher BUN/FIB (OR: 1.565; 95% CI: 1.348-1.851; P<0.001) as independently associated with 30-day mortality. BUN/FIB showed an apparent AUC of 0.835 (95% CI: 0.791-0.880), with a cohort-derived cut-off of 3.312 mmol/g. This threshold showed a sensitivity of 78.4% and specificity of 78.0% but requires external validation. BUN/FIB showed higher apparent discrimination than conventional inflammatory indices and comparable apparent discrimination with Ct-derived SFTSV RNA burden. Higher BUN/FIB was associated with poorer survival. In paired analyses, BUN/FIB decreased among survivors and increased among non-survivors. Admission BUN/FIB was independently associated with 30-day mortality and showed favorable apparent discriminatory performance in this retrospective cohort. BUN/FIB may serve as a candidate adjunctive prognostic marker, but its optimal threshold, clinical utility, and generalizability require validation in prospective multicenter studies.

title: OVER-TIME II trial: design and rationale of a multicentre randomized study evaluating antithrombotic strategies in patients with acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery ectasia.
abstract: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is characterized by diffuse coronary dilatation and increased thrombotic risk. In patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and CAE, the optimal antithrombotic strategy remains unclear. Previously, an exploratory trial suggested that the combination of antiplatelet monotherapy plus oral anticoagulation may reduce ischaemic events without increasing bleeding risk compared to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), although it was underpowered for definitive conclusions. The aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of antiplatelet monotherapy plus direct oral anticoagulation compared with DAPT in patients with ACS and culprit-vessel CAE in a multicentre randomized setting. OVER-TIME II is a multicentre, multinational, randomized, open-label clinical trial with 1:1 allocation comparing acetylsalicylic acid 100 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg vs. clopidogrel 75 mg plus rivaroxaban 15 mg daily. The study will include 326 patients with ACS and culprit-vessel CAE. Patients will be followed for 12 months. The co-primary efficacy endpoint is the time to first occurrence of a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or repeat revascularization. The co-primary safety endpoint is the time to first occurrence of major or minor bleeding defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium criteria. Secondary endpoints include individual components of the primary outcomes. Exploratory analyses will include genomic and transcriptomic profiling through DNA and RNA sampling to identify molecular signatures associated with thrombotic risk, treatment response, and clinical outcomes. OVER-TIME II is designed to provide robust multicentre randomized evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of an anticoagulation-based strategy in patients with ACS and CAE, with the potential to contribute to future clinical research and guideline development. NCT07511257. The trial is registered and publicly available on ClinicalTrials.gov and is currently actively recruiting patients.

title: Integrative molecular profiling of TAM receptors and STAT-SOCS signaling in thymic epithelial tumors.
abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare, molecularly heterogeneous tumors with a complex immune microenvironment. How TAM receptor signaling interacts with STAT-SOCS-mediated immune regulation in TETs remains incompletely understood. The TAM receptor family and STAT-SOCS signaling were examined in relation to genomic alterations, gene expression, survival, and the immune microenvironment, using TCGA-THYM genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data integrated with GTEx normal thymus expression profiles. Expression of TAM receptors (AXL, MERTK, TYRO3), their ligands (GAS6, PROS1), and the STAT1-SOCS1/SOCS3 axis was assessed using GEPIA2; survival associations were evaluated using GEPIA2 and patient-level TCGA-THYM data, and immune infiltration using TIMER2.0. Cell-type expression of TAM pathway genes was assessed using TET single-cell RNA-seq data, and protein-protein interactions using STRING. Genomic alterations affecting the TAM-STAT-SOCS axis were infrequent, comprising missense variants and copy-number amplifications. AXL, MERTK, PROS1, GAS6, STAT1, and SOCS1 showed higher expression in tumor tissues than in normal thymus. Higher MERTK expression was associated with poorer overall survival in the GEPIA2 analysis, although not significant in WHO-stratified and multivariable analyses. AXL, MERTK, and TYRO3 expression were inversely correlated with CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltration, whereas GAS6, PROS1, STAT1, and SOCS3 were positively associated with neutrophil infiltration. MERTK expression was positively correlated with CD274, and single-cell analysis showed MERTK was most frequent in macrophage/monocyte populations. TAM-STAT-SOCS expression was associated with the TET immune landscape, with MERTK showing an initial association with overall survival and further associations with T-cell infiltration, CD274 expression, and cell-type-specific expression patterns.

title: Bias-Controlled Computational Prioritisation of Therapeutic Hypotheses From Heterogeneous Molecular Data Identifies PLK1 as the Leading MTX-Combination Candidate in Choriocarcinoma.
abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) resistance remains clinically relevant in gestational trophoblastic neoplasia and choriocarcinoma. Because disease-specific molecular cohorts are limited, computational prioritisation of therapeutic hypotheses from heterogeneous public data must explicitly distinguish experimental prioritisation from therapeutic validation. Protein and phosphoprotein changes from an MTX-resistant JEG-3 model were used as effect-size seeds for random walk with restart propagation across four molecular interaction networks. Computational robustness was assessed using dropout analyses, degree-preserving edge randomisation, and seed-degree-matched permutation. Orthogonal evidence from DepMap/PRISM, external transcriptomic datasets, DrugComb records, a normal-placenta single-cell reference, and normal-tissue RNA expression was integrated to evaluate biological plausibility and translational constraints. Candidate hypotheses were prioritised using transparent multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), and cross-modal agreement was summarised descriptively using rank concordance rather than a combined-probability test, because the evidence sources share overlapping cell-cycle and DNA-damage-repair signal and therefore do not satisfy the independence assumption required by such tests. PLK1 ranked first across all 3000 MCDA perturbations, demonstrating stable prioritisation despite uncertainty in evidence weighting. Network propagation supported prioritisation but not discovery-level significance: the edge-degree-preserving empirical p value was 0.017 (BH-FDR, 0.479), and the seed-degree-matched p value was 0.048 (BH-FDR, 0.896). No candidate reached FDR significance in external transcriptomic meta-analysis or lineage- and proliferation-adjusted DepMap/PRISM regression. PLK1 was the only candidate ranked first across all four evaluated evidence analyses (both network null models, adjusted DepMap analysis, and external transcriptomic meta-analysis), indicating complete descriptive cross-modal rank concordance without assuming statistical independence across analyses. PLK1 also showed strong but nonselective basal dependency across three choriocarcinoma models. DrugComb contained one independent MTX plus PLK1-inhibitor observation with positive ZIP synergy, and the exploratory tumour-to-highest-critical-normal RNA ratio was 1.25. This bias-controlled computational prioritisation framework identifies MTX plus PLK1 inhibition as the highest-priority therapeutic hypothesis for experimental evaluation in choriocarcinoma. PARP1 and PRKDC remain secondary biomarker-stratified hypotheses. More broadly, the framework demonstrates how heterogeneous molecular data can be integrated into transparent, reproducible therapeutic hypothesis prioritisation while explicitly separating computational prioritisation from therapeutic validation.

title: Inhibition of G6PD-Mediated MAPK Signaling Triggers Mitochondrial Apoptosis and Cell Cycle Arrest in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) has been implicated in tumor progression. This study investigated the biological role of G6PD in the malignant progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and explored the underlying molecular mechanisms. RNA-sequencing data and corresponding clinical data for patients with HCC were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Independent validation datasets were obtained from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). We performed bioinformatics analyses to assess the expression of G6PD in HCC, as well as its relationship with clinical features and prognostic outcomes. Immunohistochemistry and western blotting were used to validate G6PD expression in human HCC tissues and cell lines. Stable G6PD-overexpressing and knockdown cell lines were established using lentiviral transduction. Functional assays were performed using G6PD-overexpressing and G6PD-knockdown cell lines to evaluate cell proliferation, cell cycle progression, apoptosis, mitochondrial function, and oxidative stress. Western blotting was conducted to assess the protein levels of key regulators of cell cycle progression, apoptosis, and the MAPK pathway. Finally, a BALB/c nude mouse xenograft model was used to evaluate the in vivo effects of G6PD on tumor growth. G6PD was significantly overexpressed in HCC tissues and was significantly associated with histological grade (p < 0.001), T stage (p = 0.039), vascular invasion (p = 0.002), and pathological stage (p = 0.031). Patients with high G6PD expression exhibited significantly shorter overall, disease-specific, and progression-free survival. Multivariate analysis identified high G6PD expression as an independent predictor of mortality in patients with HCC. G6PD knockdown significantly inhibited HCCLM3 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest, accompanied by the downregulation of cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4), cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6), and cyclin D1 protein levels. In addition, G6PD silencing triggered mitochondrial apoptosis, including decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, BCL-2-associated X protein (BAX) and cysteine-aspartic acid protease-3 (caspase-3) upregulation, B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) downregulation, elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and suppressed MEK1/2 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation. In vivo, G6PD knockdown significantly reduced xenograft tumor size and weight and decreased Ki67 and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) expression. G6PD is an independent prognostic biomarker in HCC and promotes disease progression through pleiotropic mechanisms, including modulation of the MAPK/ERK pathway, promotion of cell proliferation, and suppression of mitochondrial apoptosis. These findings suggest that G6PD and its downstream signaling pathways may be promising therapeutic targets for HCC.

title: Integrated time-series multi-omics reveals temporal reprogramming and inter-organ divergence in diabetic cardiorenal syndrome.
abstract: Diabetes induces progressive transcriptional reprogramming in the heart and kidney, yet their tissue-specific temporal dynamics and cellular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed a longitudinal design with dense sampling intervals, performing time-series bulk RNA-seq on heart and kidney tissues across six bi-weekly intervals from Control, high-fat diet (HF), diabetes (DM), and insulin-treated (INS) mice (n=38 total samples). To cross-validate and resolve cell-type-specific variations, these data were integrated with a public single-cell RNA-seq dataset (16 mouse kidneys) spanning Control, diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) treatment groups. Principal component analysis and differential expression sequencing revealed a more pronounced, earlier transcriptional divergence in the kidney than in the heart under diabetic conditions. Using maSigPro regression analysis, we identified 74 core time-dependent genes in the kidney; hierarchical clustering showed that the major dynamic module was enriched in immunometabolic and inflammatory pathways. Single-cell dissection localized Enpp2 upregulation within injured proximal tubule cells (Inj.PT) of the DKD group, while MHC class I molecules (H2-K1 and H2-D1) were suppressed in immune cells. UpSet plot analysis demonstrated an overlap of these dynamic hub genes between bulk and single-cell cohorts. While insulin reversed systemic metabolic and early-phase immune aberrations in the bulk cohort, the single-cell dataset-derived from an independent SGLT2i-treated cohort-provided cellular resolution for key dynamic genes (Enpp2, H2-K1, H2-D1) and suggested that SGLT2i may similarly suppress Enpp2 in injured proximal tubule cells. These parallel observations from two distinct therapeutic interventions are hypothesis-generating and warrant direct comparative studies. These discovery-phase findings were validated by independent qPCR and immunohistochemical analyses. Taken together, this exploratory longitudinal analysis identifies tissue-specific temporal transcriptional reprogramming in diabetic heart and kidney, with evidence of partial modulation by insulin treatment.

title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing.
abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood. Publicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed to characterize common biological pathways. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were used to identify and validate shared hub genes and to construct diagnostic models. Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using CIBERSORT, and the cellular localization of hub genes was further validated using scRNA-seq analysis. WGCNA identified 329 genes shared between OP- and RA-associated modules, which were significantly enriched in muscle-related processes, cytokine signaling, and immune-inflammatory pathways. RF analysis identified three shared candidate genes: ANO5, IL27RA, and CNTN3. Among these, ANO5 and IL27RA demonstrated consistent expression evidence and literature support, whereas CNTN3 emerged as a computationally nominated candidate requiring cautious interpretation and experimental validation. An SVM-based model incorporating these genes demonstrated robust predictive accuracy in both OP and RA validation cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct yet coordinated immune landscapes, with hub genes showing significant correlations with T cells, macrophages, B cells, and plasma cells. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed that ANO5 was predominantly expressed in macrophages and fibroblasts, IL27RA was mainly enriched in T cells, whereas CNTN3 showed minimal enrichment at the single-cell level in both OP bone and RA synovial tissues. This integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study identifies shared molecular signatures and immune-related mechanisms underlying OP and RA. ANO5 and IL27RA emerge as robust candidate regulators linking immune dysregulation and bone remodeling, whereas CNTN3-although identified by machine learning-requires cautious interpretation and further investigation due to limited supporting evidence. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of RA-associated OP and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for their comorbidity.

title: Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identifies Epi_C4 and Supports a Pro-Tumor Role for FAM20C in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Intratumoral epithelial heterogeneity contributes to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression and may limit the interpretability of prognostic models derived from bulk tissue. To characterize this heterogeneity and assess its clinical relevance, four public single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets comprising 193,280 quality-controlled cells were integrated. Five epithelial states were identified and characterized based on inferred aneuploidy, transcriptional programs, differentiation potential, trajectory structure, and intercellular communication. State-specific signatures were projected onto the Cancer Genome Atlas LUAD cohort and six independent Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts. Epi_C4 exhibited high inferred aneuploidy, reduced differentiation, elevated malignancy-associated program scores, and enrichment in LUAD and was associated with worse survival. A 12-gene prognostic model derived from Epi_C4 stratified patients according to overall survival in the training cohort and most validation cohorts, but not in GSE29013. High-risk tumors were enriched for extracellular matrix, PI3K-AKT, HIF-1, glycolytic, inflammatory, and immunoregulatory programs. FAM20C was enriched in Epi_C4, overexpressed in LUAD, and associated with worse survival. In NCI-H838 cells, siRNA-mediated FAM20C depletion reduced cell viability, DNA synthesis, Matrigel invasion, and wound closure while increasing apoptosis. Collectively, these findings identify Epi_C4 as a prognostically adverse epithelial state in LUAD and implicate FAM20C in tumor-associated cellular phenotypes.

title: Integrative bioinformatics, single-cell, and machine learning analyses identify OIP5-AS1 as a pro-oncogenic ceRNA hub in gastric cancer.
abstract: Despite advances in treatment, gastric cancer prognosis remains poor, necessitating the discovery of reliable molecular biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study investigates the long non-coding RNA OIP5-AS1 as a candidate oncogenic regulator through an integrated strategy combining bioinformatics, single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning, and experimental assays. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed substantial intratumoral heterogeneity across tumor layers, while integrative network analysis and machine learning prioritized OIP5-AS1 as a potential regulatory hub associated with disease progression, characterized by putative interactions with miR-20a-5p and downstream dysregulation of targets such as ZBTB4. Additional model-level prognostic contributions were observed for miR-155-5p and PTEN, although these were not included in the proposed ceRNA axis. The machine learning models further supported the discriminatory and prognostic relevance of OIP5-AS1-related features, and examination of a 30-patient clinical cohort confirmed its significant, grade-dependent overexpression in tumor tissues. Functional experiments in AGS gastric adenocarcinoma cells demonstrated that siRNA-mediated silencing of OIP5-AS1 effectively induces apoptosis, evidenced by altered BAX/BCL2 ratios and flow cytometry, while simultaneously inhibiting cancer cell migration. Collectively, these findings position OIP5-AS1 as a candidate oncogenic regulator and putative ceRNA hub in gastric cancer pathogenesis, highlighting its potential utility as a candidate prognostic biomarker and a promising avenue for targeted therapeutic intervention. However, definitive clinical utility and direct molecular binding require further validation.

title: Prognostic value of cell differentiation-related genes in follicular lymphoma based on integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing.
abstract: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the most common indolent B-cell lymphoma and follows a heterogeneous clinical course; however, reliable molecular markers for risk stratification are still lacking. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE182434) with bulk transcriptomic data from three GEO cohorts (GSE66166, GSE119214, GSE16131) and applied pseudotime trajectory analysis, consensus clustering, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and LASSO Cox regression to derive a cell differentiation-related gene signature (CDRGS) and a prognostic risk model. Model performance was evaluated by time-dependent ROC analysis, the concordance index, calibration curves, decision-curve analysis, and multivariable Cox regression, and the expression of the signature genes was examined by RT-qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry in lymphoma cell lines, in a SU-DHL-4 xenograft model, and in an independent cohort of patients with FL. Pseudotime analysis resolved three differentiation states, and consensus clustering based on the CDRGS stratified patients into three molecular subtypes with different overall survival. A three-gene model comprising SIRPG, FLT3LG, and LAG3 separated high- and low-risk patients in the training cohort and in the GSE119214 validation cohort, with separation in the same direction but not reaching significance in GSE16131, and remained associated with overall survival after adjustment for M7-FLIPI in the two cohorts in which that index was available. All three genes were expressed at higher mRNA and protein levels in lymphoma cell lines than in a non-malignant B lymphoblastoid line, indicating that the malignant cells themselves express them. In an independent patient cohort, the expression of the three-gene panel varied with risk score and with established clinical indices in the directions predicted by the model coefficients. We constructed a cell differentiation-related prognostic model for FL and found that SIRPG, FLT3LG, and LAG3 provide candidate biomarkers of the immune microenvironment that carry prognostic information beyond M7-FLIPI and merit prospective validation.
